rv.q: The piece, performed during the day for school groups and during the evening for the public, is not only serving students who've largely been starved of in-person arts education during the COVID-19 pandemic, it's a reminder of the huge power of locally oriented material.
Playwright J. Nicole Brooks’ new world premiere adaptation, now on stage at Steppenwolf Theatre Company, brings Ewing’s interweaving of research and imagination to thrilling, kinetic life.
This scorching production is co-directed by two local scholars, educators and experienced directors.

cn.t: Critics mostly praise this kinetic adaptation of Eve L. Ewing's poetry about Chicago's 1919 race riots as moving and thrilling, though one finds it too abstract. The nonlinear storytelling divides opinion.
